subject: EdgeCase AI — SLO fit, throughput targets & deployment options
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@edgecase.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgecase.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeCase AI — SLO fit, throughput targets & deployment options

Thanks for taking time today — brief recap + next steps to keep momentum.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Live inference tail latency for interactive product flows spikes to ~1.1s at 4k qps during peak hours (bad for UX).
- Cost per 1k queries is currently prohibitive for lower-margin customers; you want sub-$12 per 1k at production scale.
- Regulatory/data residency constraints for EU pilot customers (we discussed a staged approach).

Goals we heard:
1) Confirm a deployment that meets 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for single-turn prompts at 256 tokens.
2) Achieve steady-state throughput of 3k–5k qps with predictable autoscaling and warm KV cache behavior.
3) Define an MVP Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for a 6-week POC that proves SLOs and cost targets.

Technical summary / initial recommendations (high-level):
- Model & quantization: run the customer-preferred 13B variant; we recommend int8 quant for Dedicated pilot to cut token cost ~2.8x with minimal quality impact.
- Topology: hybrid routing — primary Dedicated pool in us-west with automatic fallback to hosted multi-tenant GPUs for burst (maintains SLA).
- Caching & batching: configure prefix caching for common templates; batch window target 8–12ms for throughput-critical routes.
- KV cache warmup: pre-warm strategy to avoid cold-start tail spikes for morning traffic pattern.

Action items we agreed on:
- EdgeCase: drop a 24h rolling sample of request traces + token distribution (CSV/zip) by Mon 9/21 — Samir to provide.
- Redwood: provide a tailored MAP and a cost model by Wed 9/23 (I will attach MAP workbook).
- Both: schedule a short ops deep-dive with infra (30 min) next week to align on pre-warming and autoscaling knobs.

Attachments I’m including: baseline-latency-scan.pdf (high-level latency model) and mutual-action-plan-EC042.xlsx (MAP draft). I also attached a small sample template for request traces (edgecase-load-profile.csv) — please use that format when sharing traces.

If any of this doesn't match your notes, flag it here and we'll correct. Otherwise I’ll follow up with the MAP and a proposed time for the ops call.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@edgecase.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeCase AI — SLO fit, throughput targets & deployment options

Thanks Stephanie — that lines up well. Quick clarifications from our engineering side:

- The 1.1s spike is measured at 99th percentile during an internal A/B experiment with synthetic bursts; real-world 99th settles closer to 700ms normally.
- Token distribution: ~70% of requests are <= 120 tokens; 15% between 120–400; we have a long-tail 15% that can be multipart.
- For EU pilot, we need assurance that logs/audit trails for the EU customers remain in-region; can Redwood expose region-limited audit exports?

Samir (cc’d) will upload a 48h trace dump by EOD Monday (we ran an extra capture today).

Also: a short ask — can you include a simple emulation config/example that shows how batching gains change with window size? That will help our infra team visualize tradeoffs.

Ethan
Head of Product | EdgeCase AI
ethan.cole@edgecase.ai

Subject: Re: EdgeCase AI — SLO fit, throughput targets & deployment options

Appreciate the clarifications, Ethan — good data points. A few quick technical confirmations and next steps from Redwood ops side: 

1) Region-limited audit exports: yes — for Private deployments we can enable EU-only audit export buckets (S3/GCS with customer KMS). For Hosted/Dedicated we provide filtered audit export streams and a retention policy that can be restricted by region. I’ll include a short ops note in the MAP.

2) Batching emulation: attached a 1-page PDF that demonstrates batching vs latency vs tokens per request (simple simulator). We'll also publish a runnable notebook in the shared Drive folder this week.

3) Pre-warm plan: our suggested pre-warm schedule: rolling warm for the top 20% most-common KV prefixes 30 minutes before peak + a cold-batch warming job for the rest. This avoids a large token tax on cold runs and keeps tail stable.

Next practical asks for you to unblock the MAP:
- Samir: upload traces to the Drive folder (edgecase-ec042-poc) in the CSV format Stephanie attached.
- Priya: confirm pilot customer list for EU residency (we need two org names + sample data residency requirements).

Attachments: baseline-latency-scan.pdf (same), batching-emulation-onepager.pdf (stub).

I’ll draft the MAP tasks and ownership after we get the traces.

Best,
